headline: Ford rehires veteran engineers after AI quality systems fall short
summary: The automaker is bringing back experienced staff to train AI tools and improve quality, anticipating $1 billion in cost reductions.
details: Ford executives revealed the company has rehired 350 veteran engineers, some former employees and others from suppliers, due to disappointing results from AI and automated quality systems.

Chief Operating Officer Kumar Galhotra stated that the company had been "relying more and more on automated quality systems" with suboptimal outcomes. The newly rehired "technical specialists" are tasked with identifying failure points before parts reach the assembly line.

Charles Poon, VP of vehicle hardware engineering, admitted that Ford "mistakenly thought that by just introducing artificial intelligence and ingesting the design requirements that we had, that that would produce a high-quality product."
This move does not signify an abandonment of AI initiatives. Instead, the "gray beard" engineers will mentor younger staff and assist in reprogramming the AI tools.

The strategic rehiring is projected to yield $1 billion in cost savings for Ford this year. Additionally, the automaker recently secured the top position among mainstream brands in the JD Power Initial Quality Survey.
